patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff and the tracked fixed commit only update `safe_atof()`-adjacent project code and do not touch the reproduced JSON path. Fixed-side validation therefore used the authoritative `n132/arvo:42516681-fix` image, whose untracked `fuzzer/FuzzJson.c` allocates `DataFx = calloc(Size + 1, 1)` and passes that NUL-terminated buffer into `libgps_json_unpack()`.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: the first argument supplied to `libgps_json_unpack()` is already a NUL-terminated C string
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `libgps_json_unpack((char *)Data, &gpsdata, NULL)` executes, the buffer handed to the JSON decoder must already be a valid C string with an in-bounds terminating `\0`, because the selected ERROR path later scans that same buffer with `strstr`, `str_starts_with`, and `json_internal_read_object()` using raw C-string semantics.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable harness forwards the raw 23-byte fuzz buffer directly, so the parser receives no terminator inside the provided span. The authoritative fixed image first allocates `DataFx = calloc(Size + 1, 1)` and passes `DataFx`, making the same harness-to-library call site deliver a real NUL-terminated string while still reaching the parser loop.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original records `json_unpack_call.call_buffer_is_c_string=0` and still reaches `object_loop_guard`. The authoritative fixed image records `json_unpack_call.call_buffer_is_c_string=1` at the same source-level call site and still reaches `object_loop_guard`, so the required assertion is genuinely satisfied on the fixed side without perturbation.

nodes.state: At the start of the generic object-parser loop, local cursor `cp` is the exact buffer pointer previously supplied by the harness to `libgps_json_unpack()`, so the parser begins scanning that caller-provided byte span from its first byte.
nodes.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace records `json_unpack_call.json_buffer_ptr == object_scan_entry.scan_cursor_ptr == 0x7f36028fd800`; the fixed trace records the same equality with `0x603000000010`.

nodes.state: At the immediate pre-sink loop-guard checkpoint, `cp` has advanced from the buffer start to the tracked end slot that the next `*cp` evaluation will inspect. On the vulnerable original this slot is the first user-poisoned byte after the 23-byte witness; on the fixed harness it is the added NUL terminator.
nodes.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace records `object_scan_entry.scan_cursor_ptr=0x7f36028fd800` and `object_loop_guard.scan_cursor_ptr=0x7f36028fd817`, matching the saved ASan report's poisoned offset 23 bytes into the input region.

edges.relation: The same byte buffer passed as the first argument to `libgps_json_unpack()` becomes `json_internal_read_object()`'s local cursor `cp` when the ERROR path reaches the generic object parser.
edges.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace records `json_unpack_call.json_buffer_ptr == object_scan_entry.scan_cursor_ptr == 0x7f36028fd800`; the fixed trace records the same equality with `0x603000000010`.

edges.relation: The same parser cursor `cp` that starts at the first byte of the JSON buffer advances through the truncated second attribute until the next loop-guard re-evaluation on the tracked boundary slot.
edges.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace records `object_scan_entry.scan_cursor_ptr=0x7f36028fd800` and `object_loop_guard.scan_cursor_ptr=0x7f36028fd817`; the fixed trace records the analogous start/end pair `0x603000000010` -> `0x603000000027` on the clean run.
